name: Kunsthalle Mannheim
funding: City of Mannheim, Hans-Werner and Josephine Hector (€50M for the Hector building) and their foundations, the Förderkreis, and a Stifterkreis of 57 persons, foundations and firms.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; support pages name the Hector family and foundations, and the Stifterkreis page lists the foundation council and executive board, undated.

name: Ballroom Marfa
funding: No donor list is published; the site credits 'individuals and foundations' without names. The FY2023 filing shows $589K in contributions on $818K revenue and $1.13M expenses.
watch: Free public admission; governance guidelines prohibit fossil extraction or defense underwriting despite local geographic oil economy.
records_note: Its People page names 22 trustees, ProPublica holds Form 990s for 2004 to 2023, and a 20th Anniversary Fund donor page names about 38 givers.

name: Chinati Foundation
watch: Founded by Donald Judd in Marfa, Texas. Preserves large-scale installations across 340 acres.
records_note: Its Financial Information page posts audited statements and Form 990s for 2016 to 2024, and a Trustees page names 19; it names no donors.

name: Judd Foundation
funding: FY2025-26 supporters include Bloomberg Philanthropies, Texas Commission on the Arts, Henry Moore Foundation, Japan Foundation, Villa Albertine, Neuberger Berman, Gagosian and Bristol Myers Squibb, plus many patrons and individuals.
watch: Maintains Donald Judd's permanently installed living and working spaces in Marfa and 101 Spring Street, New York.
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies is campaigned against elsewhere, not at Judd. Contributions were $966K of $12.6M revenue in FY2025.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990 filings are on ProPublica, a named supporters list is published each year to FY2025, and the board is listed.

name: MACAAL
funding: Fondation Alliances, set up in 2009 by Othman Lazraq, funds it. The Lazraq family runs the listed property developer Alliances. No other funder is named.
watch: Museum of African Contemporary Art Al Maaden in Marrakech.
records_note: MACAAL's site covers exhibitions, mission and visits, and links its founder, Fondation Alliances, but posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: ACCA
funding: Creative Victoria, Creative Australia and the City of Melbourne, plus the Ian Potter Foundation. Corporate partners include Dulux, KWM, Wood Marsh, Supernormal and Hannah St Hotel.
watch: Australian Centre for Contemporary Art in Melbourne.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2018 and names supporters and its board in the 2025 report, but the report carries no financial statements.

name: Heide Museum of Modern Art
funding: Creative Victoria, Creative Australia and Manningham Council. Tucker, Gordon Darling, Downer and Shine On foundations; North East Link Community Fund; Melbourne Water; law, design and media sponsors.
watch: Established at the former home of John and Sunday Reed in Bulleen, Victoria.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2003 and audited 2024 accounts, names donors in its 2024 report and lists its seven-member board.

name: Museo Jumex
funding: Fundación Jumex runs the museum with no board, funded by profits of the Grupo Jumex juice company. Admission is free.
watch: Corporate Underwritten: Located in Mexico City's Polanco district. Free admission to the public; operational budget is derived from the Grupo Jumex beverage manufacturing conglomerate under family foundation governance.
why_flagged: Fundación Jumex runs the museum with no board, funded by profits of the Grupo Jumex juice company. Admission is free.
records_note: The museum's foundation posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; the site names only Grupo Jumex as the source of support.

name: Museo Tamayo
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; the foundation page names its board and international council, while corporate sponsors appear as undated logos.

name: ICA Miami
funding: $15.3M contributions (FY2025), free admission. Partners are Knight Foundation, City National Bank, Miami Design District and Cartier. Irma Braman co-chairs the board.
watch: Located in the Miami Design District with permanent free admission.
why_flagged: Executive committee member Alex Witkoff co-founded World Liberty Financial, the Trump family crypto firm, which faces conflict-of-interest scrutiny.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s are on ProPublica, the About page shows four undated partner logos with role labels, and trustees are listed.

name: MIMA
funding: Teesside University unit. 2024-25 funders: Arts Council England, Middlesbrough Council, Freelands Foundation, Contemporary Art Society, Henry Moore Foundation, AHRC, Art Fund, Holiday Action Fund.
watch: Roster from the 2024-25 impact report. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: A Teesside University unit: one impact report (2024-25) names funders; the university publishes accounts 2002 to 2025 and lists its governors.

name: Fondazione Prada
funding: Chaired by Miuccia Prada. 2019 revenue was €25.2M from tickets, catalogues and sponsorship contracts; it received no donations that year.
watch: Corporate Underwritten: Major private cultural institution funded by Italian luxury fashion house Prada. While maintaining visionary curatorial integrity and international acclaim, operational governance and capital investments are tied to commercial luxury corporate revenues.
why_flagged: Prada withdrew its Pradamalia figurines in December 2018 after blackface criticism and boycott calls. No flagged funder and no protest at the foundation found.
records_note: Posts an institutional report covering 2017 to 2019 with summary financials and its board; it names no sponsors and reports no donations in 2018.
